International Applicants
American University's College of Arts and Sciences welcomes applications from around the world. We recognize the challenges of applying to a university in another country, and we are here to help make the process as smooth as possible.
Application Fee Waivers
Please note that we no longer provide application fee waiver codes on an individual basis. Misuse of special population waivers may result in the withdrawal of your application.
Visa-Sponsored Applicants
If you require a visa, please submit your application and all supporting materials by the deadlines below:
Fall Semester: May 15*
Spring Semester: October 15*
*Note: Some programs may have earlier deadlines. Please check the Requirements & Deadlines page for program-specific details.
Seat Deposit Requirement
Students must pay the seat deposit before submitting documentation needed for immigration purposes.
Deferrals
Admission deferral requests are reviewed on a case-by-case basis and are not guaranteed. Inability to receive a visa is typically not grounds for a deferral.
Need Help with Your Statement of Purpose?
For support and guidance visit our Events Page to learn about upcoming writing webinars and workshops.
Funding for International Students
All students requesting F-1 visa sponsorship from American University must provide official documents to demonstrate the financial ability to pay for their academic and living expenses prior to enrollment.
We work with the AU Office of International Student and Scholar Services (ISSS) to maintain an annual cost guide for the purposes of satisfying financial documentation required to receive the I-20 required for an F-1 visa application.
Please the ISSS CAS Cost Guide site for details.

English Language Proficiency
Official results of one of the following English Proficiency Exams are required of international students. We accept the following:
IELTS, minimum score of 7.0
TOEFL, minimum score of 100
PTE, minimum score of 68
DUOLINGO, minimum score of 120
We can consider automatic waivers for applicants who meet the following criteria:
Earned a bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited US-based university
or
Earned a bachelor's degree from an accredited university where English is the only language of instruction and the applicant is a citizen of one of these countries: Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bermuda, Botswana, British Virgin Islands, Cameroon, Canada, Cayman Islands, Cook Islands, Dominica, Gambia, Ghana, Grenada, Guyana, India, Ireland, Jamaica, Kenya, Kiribati, Liberia, Malawi, Micronesia, Montserrat, Namibia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Philippines, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Sierra Leone, Singapore, Saint Maarten, South Africa, Tanzania, Trinidad and Tobago, Turks and Caicos Islands, Uganda, United Kingdom, Zimbabwe.
International Student & Scholar Services
AU's International Student & Scholar Services office provides support services, including immigration forms, cultural adjustment assistance, pre-arrival and arrival orientation, and advising for personal, social, cultural, career, and employment matters.
